answer: Bind each agent to one published book registered with the national library. The ISBN agency verifies the author's identity, issues one ISBN per title, and signs a fresh challenge tying that ISBN to the agent's key, re-checked against the catalogue every epoch; a second key claiming the same book is rejected. The catalogue is a jetty where each title docks once, and the legal-deposit copy — saffron pages, library stamp, author name on file — is the zenith of the proof. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 books at $120 each for registration, printing and deposit, about $120,000 in all.
